outcome: Consolidated R3 Claude Low: pre-existing thread/unarchive Timeout/Transport may mean the remote operation completed or is still pending, while local thread state/release remain Archived. Source evidence: codex_thread_actions.rs unarchive RPC returns early on error; delegation_followup_admission.rs rollback checks Restored. Do not infer no restore from absence in archived inventory or from an immediate archived sample: the original RPC may complete later. acceptance: A Codex thread/unarchive timeout or transport failure retains typed ambiguity bound to the exact session, thread, runtime origin and restore owner. Before retrying, the host positively reconciles the restore outcome; absence from archived inventory, an immediate archived sample or a failed probe does not prove that the original operation cannot complete later.

A rejected, unadmitted follow-up or evaluator reuse explicitly disposes of its exact prepared attempt as undelivered or withheld, retaining durable attempt identity and history. Ambiguous or admitted brief delivery remains fenced; retries do not duplicate a brief, provider command or attempt key.

A matching late unarchive completion permits only cleanup or recovery owned by that exact attempt. Manual restore, Stop or Cancel, a changed thread or runtime, an admitted successor, persistence failure and restart cannot authorize stale compensation or resurrection.

Deterministic fail-first regressions cover lost replies with late completion, positive Active reconciliation, definitive rejection, a live origin with an archived sample, an orphaned evaluator preparation, a follow-up to a completed delegation whose unarchive times out, preservation of the previous terminal result and duplicate callbacks. The maintained full gate passes on the exact final tree with a clean independent Codex and Claude review pair.
